documents.title: Generative AI @ WCU - A Guiding Framework
documents.summary: A long university framework from IS&T and the Teaching & Learning Center with six recommendations (follow policies, protect data, equity, verify accuracy, be transparent, keep informed). It is a living set of recommendations, not a policy, and tells faculty to state their own AI expectations.
documents.stance_why: The page says "This framework is a living document, not a university policy" and sets no ban or permission itself; it tells faculty to be "transparent about their expectations" and lets each instructor choose, even a complete prohibition, so the decision is delegated.

units.why: The page says "This framework is a living document, not a university policy", which fixes the status of every recommendation in it. I code it P108 (no formal AI policy here) rather than P54 because the point is its non-policy status.
units.anchor: This framework is a living document, not a university policy.
units.frag_start: This framework is a living document,
units.fit_note: The document does not say the university has no AI policy; it says this framework is recommendations that work alongside existing policies.

units.why: The purpose sentence gives "guidance on the responsible and ethical uses of generative artificial intelligence", an institution-level statement of purpose, so P56 (framework) fits better than P61 (definitions).
units.anchor: guidance on the responsible and ethical uses of generative artificial intelligence
units.frag_start: provide the West Chester University community

units.why: The recommendations "apply to all members of the university community, including students, faculty, and staff", which sets who the framework covers; P56 holds scope statements.
units.anchor: apply to all members of the university community, including students, faculty, and staff

units.why: The guidance "will be periodically reviewed and updated", a commitment to revisit it, so P54 and phase over-time.

units.why: "Comments, feedback, and suggested changes can be submitted" invites feedback on the framework, which P54 includes.

units.why: Defines AI as "the ability of a computer system to perform tasks that typically require human intelligence", a definition that sets what the framework covers (P61).

units.fit_note: Also names Alexa and Siri as AI, without saying whether embedded features fall under any rule.

documents.title: TLC Sample AI Syllabus Statements 2025
documents.summary: Teaching & Learning Center menu of optional sample syllabus statements, from use with acknowledgement to no use, plus two First Year Experience statements and department examples (Nursing, Educational Leadership). Instructors adapt them to their own courses.
documents.stance_why: The center calls the statements "optional sample syllabus statements to help you craft your own Generative AI policies" and offers five levels from "Use with Acknowledgement" to "No Use", so the document sets no stance of its own and lists tiers.

units.why: The center calls these "optional sample syllabus statements to help you craft your own Generative AI policies", sample language for instructors to adopt, P110.
units.anchor: optional sample syllabus statements to help you craft your own Generative AI policies
units.frag_start: The Teaching & Learning Center prepared these

units.why: The contents list names generic levels: "Use with Acknowledgement", "Use with Permission", "Use for Editing Only"; a set of tiers of AI use, P05.
units.anchor: 1. Use with Acknowledgement 2. Use with Permission 3. Use for Editing Only
units.fit_note: Five generic levels: acknowledgement, permission, editing only, idea generation only, no use.

units.why: "We encourage you to review 2025 AI Syllabus Statement Considerations as you select and craft a statement" points instructors to further guidance, P115.
units.anchor: We encourage you to review 2025 AI Syllabus Statement Considerations
